unitarian.trinity:
Unitarian Christians hold to the unity of God: God is one, and that one God is the Father. Jesus is honored by many as the Messiah, a teacher and an example to follow, but is not held to be a second person within the Godhead. Unitarian Christians commonly say that the doctrine of the Trinity is not stated in so many words in Scripture and took shape later, and that the simpler confession of one God is the more faithful one.

There is real variety under this name. Some historic Unitarians saw Christ as a uniquely exalted human being, others as a created but pre-existent being. Many people who use the label today belong to communities that welcome people of several faiths. Across these differences, conscience, reason and the moral teaching of Jesus generally carry more weight than creeds.
